messages:
Arun: quick sync 1: ran an "ensemble-lite" speculative head on nova-13b-quant to measure latency vs human-rated quality. goal: see if 2-stage cheap-head + quant decode keeps humans happy for QA and RAG snippets.
Sofia: awesome. what exactly is "ensemble-lite" here?
Arun: it's two tiny classifiers run in parallel: a unigram+LM-probe for continuity and a token-level surprisal head. if both agree "low surprise" we route to int8 decode with prefill; else fallback to fp16.
Evelyn: how did you collect human labels? which rubric?
Arun: we used a small raters batch (n=120) via the internal labelling app. rubric: correctness (0/1), fluency (1-5), hallucination flag (Y/N). each item reviewed by 3 raters; majority for correctness, mean for fluency.
Sofia: sample selection? we need to avoid head-inflation on super-easy prompts.
Arun: split: 40% short QA (<32 tokens), 30% RAG snippets (doc-context problems), 30% adversarial (paraphrase + missing context). also included 40 synthetic hallucination probes.
Evelyn: numbers?
Arun: latency: p50 token latency down 29% vs baseline. p95 down 18%. throughput up 21% for short QA. quality: aggregated correctness delta = -0.7% absolute (not statistically significant, p=0.12). fluency mean delta -0.05. hallucination rate +0.6% on adversarial slice.
Sofia: +0.6 hallucinations on adversarial looks marginal. CI?
Arun: 95% CI for hallucination delta is [0.1, 1.1] so borderline.
QA-bot: note: flagged 6 cases where quant-run produced exact-match but different tokenization causing evaluation mismatch; verified by manual check -> 4/6 were tokenization artefacts.
Evelyn: did we run a forced-quant holdout to bound worst-case harm?
Arun: yes. forced-quant worst-case correctness delta -1.8%, hallucination +1.7%. shows handshake helps.
Sofia: good. what's the runtime config you used? paste the command and the ensemble logic.
Arun: command: 
```\npython rrunner/eval_harness.py \
  --model nova-13b-quant \
  --evalset redwood-rag-5k \
  --speculative ensemble-lite \
  --spec-thresh 0.85 \
  --batch 1 --max_tokens 128 --streams 4
```\nArun: simplified ensemble logic: 
```\ndef ensemble_lite(prefix):\n  u = unigram_probe.score(prefix[-6:])\n  s = surprisal_head.estimate(prefix)\n  return (u.confidence > 0.9) and (s.mean < thresh)\n```\nSofia: nice. any runtime safety mitigations? kv tagging, streaming boundaries?
Arun: tagged kv with run-id, double-checked streaming flush logic (we wait for first quant token commit before sending chunk). added mismatch telemetry to ops.
ops-bot: canary scheduled: dedicated-pool-7, 2h window, 5% traffic, rollout id rh-ens-lite-1777. metrics to /dash/ens-lite-1777 every 10s.
Evelyn: next steps: 1) run larger rater cohort (n=600) prioritized on adversarial and RAG slices; 2) create synthetic perturbation sweep (typos, OOV tokens) to stress tokenization; 3) add token-level alignment checks to auto-detect tokenization artefacts.
Sofia: please include bucketed metrics by prompt length (<32, 32-128, >128) and by context type (RAG vs QA vs adversarial).
Arun: will run overnight 600-rater pass and post CSV. attaching quick stat snapshot (lat_p50,lat_p95,throughput,correct%,halluc%): 38ms, 160ms, +21%, 89.3, 3.6 vs baseline 54ms, 195ms, baseline, 90.0, 3.0
Evelyn: sounds promising. if 600-rater results show hallucination delta <0.5% and tokenization fixes reduce artefacts, green to 5% canary.
Arun: ack. I'll also dump per-rater variance so we can sanity-check rater consistency.
QA-bot: reminder: include task instructions and example gold answers in the rater bundle. missing gold answers -> invalidated votes.
ops-bot: telemetry: will emit mismatch_alerts if token-level drift > 0.3% for two consecutive 1m buckets.
Arun: thanks all. posting full run when available (~8h).
